Here's a description of the provided plot, following the guidelines:

The plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and accuracy for three different conditions. The x-axis is labeled “Initial Confidence” and has a linear scale ranging from 0.91 to 0.98, with tick labels at intervals of 0.01. The y-axis is labeled “Accuracy” and has a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick labels at intervals of 0.2. There are three lines displayed: a blue line with circular markers and a solid style, starting at approximately 0.83 at x=0.91 and ending at approximately 0.94 at x=0.98; an orange line with diamond markers and a dashed style, starting at approximately 0.63 at x=0.91 and ending at approximately 0.22 at x=0.98; and a green line with square markers and a dash-dot style, starting at approximately 0.11 at x=0.91 and ending at approximately 0.71 at x=0.98. Each line is accompanied by error bars indicating variability, with the length of the error bars changing along the x-axis.
